hero.title: Building Glass Cleaning & Façade Maintenance
hero.body: Glass cleaning, sealant replacement, repairs, and repainting for multi-storey façades by rope access — reaching areas a gondola cannot, with no permanent installation.

card.summary: Glass cleaning, sealant replacement, repairs, and repainting for multi-storey façades by rope access — reaching areas a gondola cannot, with no permanent installation.

sections.body:
## Why rope access for façades

A gondola needs rails and a permanent rooftop installation, and often cannot reach façade recesses, canopies, or narrow elevations. Rope access only needs suitable anchor points: systems are rigged within hours, move quickly between elevations, and disturb occupants no longer than necessary.

## Protecting occupants and pedestrians

The area below the work zone is cordoned off and signed, tools are tethered against drops, and every team works with a supervisor and a rescue plan. For fully occupied buildings, work can be scheduled outside peak hours.

## Planned maintenance

Glass cleaned regularly and sealant replaced on time prevent permanent staining, water ingress, and frame damage. We can set up a planned maintenance schedule — monthly, quarterly, or yearly — to suit the building.

columns.title: Scope of work
items: Replacing and re-sealing glazing and façade joints
Treating leaks and waterproofing external walls
Visual façade inspection with photo records

sections.title: Four steps from survey to report

items.title: 1. Survey & quotation
items.text: We review the site or your photos and drawings, then send the scope, method, schedule, and a written quotation.

items.title: 2. Work plan & permits
items.text: A risk assessment, method statement, and rescue plan are prepared before work starts; permits are arranged with the site manager.

items.title: 3. Delivery
items.text: A team of Kemnaker-certified technicians works with a supervisor on site; the area below the work zone is secured.

items.title: 4. Report & handover
items.text: Before-and-after photos and a work report are handed over with recommendations for the next maintenance cycle.

items.q: How often should building glass be cleaned?
items.a: Typically every 3–6 months, depending on location, pollution, and glass type. Buildings near main roads or industrial areas usually need it more often. We can recommend a schedule after seeing the building.

items.q: Is rope access as safe as a gondola?
items.a: Rope access uses two independent rope systems — a working line and a safety line — so the failure of one does not result in a fall. With certified technicians, a rescue plan, and equipment checked every day, it is a very safe method for façade work.

items.q: Does the area below have to be closed?
items.a: The area directly below the work zone is cordoned off while work is under way. The cordon moves with the team, so the building stays accessible.

items.q: Can you work outside office hours?
items.a: Yes. For busy buildings, work can be scheduled early in the morning, at weekends, or outside operating hours, as long as weather and light are safe.

sections.title: Tell us about the job
sections.text: Send the location, the type of building or asset, and your target dates. We reply with a written quotation, usually the same working day.
